 Order

Petitioner in Crl.M.C.No.6004 of 2021 is the accused in C.C.No.637 of 2019 pending before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Tripunithura alleging commission of offences under Sections 418, 420 and 495 of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Tripunithura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The same petitioner is the petitioner in Crl.M.C.
No.1295 of 2016 which has been filed seeking to quash all further proceedings in C.C.No.1569 of 2015 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Tripunithura alleging commission of offences under Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code.
2.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Tripunithura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: When this matter is taken up for consideration today, learned counsel appearing for the petitioner would submit that the cases came to be registered on account of matrimonial disputes between the petitioner and his wife [who is the defacto complainant in both cases].
It is submitted Crl.M.C.Nos.1295 of 2016 & 6004 of 2021 that all disputes between the petitioner and the defacto complainant have been settled in mediation conducted before this Court.

It is submitted that in terms of the mediation agreement, it is agreed that the proceedings in C.C.No.637 of 2019 and C.C.No.1569 of 2015, both pending before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Tripunithura,
can be quashed.

entities.text: Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Tripunithura
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 3. Heard the learned Public Prosecutor also.

Clause 7 of the memorandum of settlement executed between the petitioner and the defacto complainant in both cases under Section 89 of the Code of the Civil Procedure read with Rules 24 and 25 of the Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005 reads as follows:
"7.

The respondent further agrees that she has no objection in the Crl.M.C.6004/2021 and Crl.M.C.No.1295/16 being allowed and consequently quashing CC 637/2019 and CC 1569/2015 respectively pending before JFCM Tripunithura.
On receipt of the final settlement amount the respondent will hand over the 'no objection affidavit' to the petitioner's counsel."
Considering the fact that all disputes between the petitioner and the defacto complainant have settled in mediation, I am of the opinion that these Crl.M.Cs can be allowed.
Accordingly, C.C.No.637 of 2019 and C.C.No.1569 of 2015, both pending before the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court, Tripunithura stands quashed against the petitioner.
